messages:
Ajay (Sales): FYI Acme just sent their security questionnaire + a committed throughput ask for the enterprise deal. They want 2k rps at 512 tokens median with 95th p99 latency <= 250ms. Also asked about nightly preheat and burst credits.
Maria (SE): @Ajay thanks. Quick Q: is the 2k rps steady or spiky? any diurnal curve? sample payload size?
Beth (Acme Corp): Traffic will be spiky. baseline ~400rps, spikes up to 2k for ~10-15m, 5x/day. Prompts avg 420 tokens including context.
Kai (Infra Eng): Ok. For p99 250ms at 2k with 420 tokens we need reserved capacity + preheat. If using A100-ish instances we'd estimate ~8 reserved GPUs (quantized) + 2 burst GPUs. Preheat window ~12-15m to populate KV caches.
Maria (SE): Model matters a lot — are they open to a 7B quantized variant? That cuts GPU requirements ~2-3x vs fp16 70B.
Beth (Acme Corp): They're fine with 7B Q8 if quality checks pass. Pricing question: does quantized model change commit pricing?
Nina (Solutions): Pricing: commit is capacity-based (vGPU-hours) + per-token usage for hosted bursts. Quantized models lower vGPU-hours for same throughput -> we can reflect in proposal as a lower effective unit. I'll draft numbers.
Ajay (Sales): Also they asked about SLA degradation during AZ failures — need clear fallback plan.
Kai (Infra Eng): Recommended plan: reserved pool in two AZs with cross-AZ fallback and a standby lower-cost variant (smaller model) for graceful degradation. We'll have autoscale policy + hedging.
Maria (SE): Example autoscale snippet for their POC config:
```yaml
autoscale:
  target_rps: 2000
  min_reserved_gpus: 6
  max_reserved_gpus: 12
  preheat_window_seconds: 900
  burst_pool: 2
  fallback_model: "7B-q8-lowmem"
  canary: { percent: 10, duration: 300 }
```
Nina (Solutions): Also flag: security questionnaire requires KMS key ownership + audit logs retention 90d. Beth, can you confirm if Acme needs customer-managed KMS?
Beth (Acme Corp): Yes, customer-managed KMS required. Also they want proof of no cross-tenant KV leakage and certs for on-prem option.
Kai (Infra Eng): For KMS + audit we need a Private deployment offer or Dedicated with VPC peering + CMK. That changes onboarding timeline (add ~3 weeks) and impacts pricing.
Ajay (Sales): Timeline constraint: they want POC in 3 weeks. Is Dedicated + CMK doable?
Maria (SE): Three weeks is tight but possible if we use Dedicated with pre-provisioned GPUs and skip full on-prem. We can enable CMK and shorter retention for logs initially, then tighten after POC. Needs signoff from Security.
Nina (Solutions): I'll run the security questionnaire answers and list the gating items. Quick checklist: CMK yes, audit retention setting, network isolation, certs for on-prem, SOC2 attestation.
Beth (Acme Corp): Great. One more: how do you handle billing if spikes exceed reserved during POC?
Ajay (Sales): Billing: reserved covers baseline; bursts billed at higher per-token rate. We can include a capped burst budget for POC (e.g., $X/day) to avoid surprises.
Maria (SE): Operational note: preheat should target the hot prefix set they expect. If they have session affinity, KV cache hit rate improves dramatically. We'll need sample session IDs and distribution to simulate.
Kai (Infra Eng): Also recommend a lightweight runbook for the on-call during the POC: steps to increase burst pool, how to toggle fallback model, contact list. I'll draft.
deploy-bot: deploy started for dedicated-poc:deploy-17677 — reserved pool provisioning in progress :rocket:
Ajay (Sales): Action items: 1) @Maria simulate with Acme traffic profile and confirm GPU count + perf numbers. 2) @Nina draft sec questionnaire answers and note gating items. 3) @Kai prepare runbook + AZ config. 4) I'll put capped burst budget into the commercial proposal. Aim to have a one-pager by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
